One guardian. Four duties for your Postgres and MySQL.

01 · Watches

Eyes on every query.

Slow-query insight from pg_stat_statements or the MySQL slow log, ranked by cost. Regression alerts against each query's baseline. Index recommendations applied with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on Postgres. Schema watch for changes and drift.

03 · Protects

Guards every path in.

Read-only by default. Writes need a role and a two-step confirm. DROP and TRUNCATE are blocked over MCP. Roles, Google SSO and protected columns. Schema Guardian flags risky DDL and suggests safer paths.

Protection that matches the code. Here is what DeepSQL enforces today. No certifications are claimed.

Read-only by default

Agents read. They don't write.

A SQL guard keeps agent and generated SQL read-only and blocks dangerous functions. MCP agents never receive credentials.

DeepSQL · Gateway
SELECT … FROM ordersread-only, allowed SELECT pg_read_file(…)dangerous function INSERT INTO orders …needs role + confirm TRUNCATE ordersblocked over MCP
MCP agents never receive database credentials
Writes

Writes wait for a person.

Writes need EXECUTE_WRITES or EXECUTE_DDL and a two-step confirm. DROP and TRUNCATE are blocked over MCP.

DeepSQL · Approval
agent-7 via MCP · orders-prod
UPDATE orders SET status = 'void' WHERE id = 4182;waiting
1 Review ✓ · 2 Confirm · needs EXECUTE_WRITESConfirm
DROP TABLE orders;blocked over MCP

Book a demo
Where does DeepSQL run?

In your infrastructure: a Linux box, an EC2 instance or a container in your VPC.

Which databases does it guard?

PostgreSQL and MySQL, including databases behind a bastion over an SSH tunnel.

Which models can it use?

OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, a LiteLLM proxy, or a model on your own hardware through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

Do agents get database credentials?

No. Agents call DeepSQL, and DeepSQL holds the connection.
